items.text: The patient's or legal representative's approval and consent to being hospitalized is recorded in the patient record.
Patient education activities are recorded in the patient's medical record.
A new consent is recorded in the patient's medical record when indicated.
Informed refusal form is recorded and kept in the patient's medical record.
Patient needs and preferences are documented in the patient's medical record.
The patient's identifiers are recorded in the patient's medical record.
When patient care is required during the admission process, the care plan is recorded in the patient's medical record.
The patient's medical record identifies the physician responsible for care.
The process of requesting, communicating, and responding to second opinion requests is recorded in the patient's medical record.
Information exchange between consultation requestor and responder to consultation requests is comprehensive and recorded in the patient's medical record.
Information exchange between multidisciplinary management teams describes the patient's conditions and important findings and is recorded in the patient's medical record.
Requirements for transporting patients in critical conditions are identified, used, and recorded in the patient's medical record.
The discharge, temporary discharge, referral, and/or transfer-out orders are clearly recorded in the patient's medical record.
The referral feedback is reviewed, signed, and recorded in the patient's medical record.
A copy of the discharge summary is kept in the patient's medical record.
Pre-hospital care records are complete and kept in the patient's medical record.
Medical records of emergency patients include items from i) to viii) in the intent.
The assessment and reassessment are recorded in the patient's medical records.
The plans of care and follow-up instructions are recorded in the patient's medical records.
Initial medical assessments are performed within 24 hours of hospitalization or more frequently as per patient needs and recorded in the patient's medical record.
Medical reassessments are performed, as per the policy, and recorded in the patient's medical record.
Nurses' assessment and reassessment are timely recorded in the medical records.
Pain screening, assessment, pain management plan, and reassessment are documented in the patient records.
The hospital assesses and reassesses all inpatients for risk of fall using appropriate tools suitable for the patient population and documented in the patient's medical records.
General measures and tailored care plans (fall prevention) are recorded in the patient's medical record.
General measures and tailored care plans (pressure injury) are recorded in the patient's medical record.
Tailored care plans based on individual patient VTE risk assessments are conducted and recorded in the patient files.
The patient's nutritional needs assessment and management is recorded in the patient's medical record.
Special patient populations' needs assessment, and management is recorded in the patient's medical record.
The plan of care addresses all the elements mentioned in the intent from a) to g) and is documented in the patient medical record.
Indication for transfusion is recorded in the patient's medical record.
Monitoring of the patient's condition during transfusion is recorded in the patient's medical record.
Recognition and response to clinical deterioration are recorded in the patient's medical record.
Assessment, plan of care, and monitoring of progress are documented in the patient's medical record.
Management and use of tubes and catheters are recorded in patient medical records.
Terminally ill patients' assessment, reassessment, and management are recorded in the patient's medical record.
Management of cardio-pulmonary arrests is recorded in the patient's medical record.
Assessment, plan of care, monitoring of progress, and discharge instructions are documented in the patient's medical record.
Assessment, plan of care, and monitoring of progress are documented in the patient's medical record.
Assessment, reassessment, plan of care, CTG (cardiotocography), Partogram, pain management, and delivery summary are documented in the patient's medical record.
Assessment, plan of care, and monitoring of progress are documented in the patient's medical record.
Restraints and seclusions are recorded in the patient's medical record.
Assessment, plan of care, and monitoring of progress are documented in the patient's medical record.
Pre-transplantation evaluation and post-transplantation care plan are recorded in the patient's medical record.
When an additional or substituted examination is called for, medical imaging diagnostic service staff member informs patients and referrers and documents it in the patient's medical record.
Complete medical imaging and ancillary studies are recorded in the patient's medical record.
The identified risks of the patient's conditions are documented in the patient's medical record before surgery or invasive procedure.
The focused assessment is documented in the patient's medical record.
The report is kept in the patient's medical record.
The examination results are available in the patient's medical record within the defined time frame.
The pre-anesthesia assessment and the anesthesia plan are recorded in the patient's medical record.
Immediate pre-induction assessment is performed by the anesthesiologist and recorded in the patient's medical record.
The results of the monitoring are recorded in the patient's medical record regularly according to the approved professional practice guidelines/protocols.
The implemented anesthesia care is recorded in the patient's medical record, including all elements from a) to k) in the intent.
A copy of the anesthesia record is kept in the patient's medical record.
The patient's physiologic status is monitored during post-anesthesia care, according to professional practice guidelines, and recorded in the patient's medical record.
The provided post-anesthesia care from a) to k) in the intent is recorded in the patient's medical record.
The pre-procedural sedation assessment and the procedural sedation plan are recorded in the patient's medical record.
Procedural sedation record is kept in the patient's medical record.
The provided post-procedural sedation care is recorded in the patient's medical record, including items from a) to g) in the intent.
Signed patient consent for participation in research is placed in the research file and the patient's medical record.
